bug_semantics: An authenticated member who can edit a shared workflow can put a credential ID belonging to another user into an HTTP Request node and make genericAuthType (or the analogous nodeCredentialType) an expression that resolves to the real credential type only at execution time. CredentialsPermissionChecker statically computes active credential types from unresolved node parameters. The expression text is not equal to the credential object's real type key, so mapCredIdsToNodes drops the referenced credential and the project ownership/access query never sees its ID. The HTTP Request runtime later resolves the expression and loads that credential, allowing its use or exfiltration; the attacker must know the victim credential ID.
flaw_origin: The smallest source commit is PR #25599 member 7d6023fe3478df86d88f3602f1ea5b53819a050b. It changed mapCredIdsToNodes from unconditionally mapping every node.credentials value to first computing getActiveCredentialTypes and then continuing past any credential whose type is not in that statically derived set. The new helper evaluated display conditions and copied the unresolved nodeCredentialType string, but did not fail closed for expressions. That created the authorization gap: an expression-selected credential could be active at runtime yet absent from the pre-execution permission query. The public squash merge 608e3bf214328e679c03da3e4a6e9c22ceaac9ca is not the smallest BIC; GitHub's public PR-commits endpoint reconstructs its two source commits. Later bundle 2d9a2ec76e180b54e8091e31b1e0638c909abd99 added raw genericAuthType to the same set, preserving rather than originating the expression mismatch.

GET /repos/n8n-io/n8n/commits/7d6023fe3478df86d88f3602f1ea5b53819a050b reports author and committer Guillaume Jacquart <jacquart.guillaume@gmail.com> and the complete message 'refine credential access check to discard not actively used credentials'; there is no Co-authored-by, Generated-with, AI trailer, AI identity, or bot identity. evidence: Advisory: GET /repos/n8n-io/n8n/security-advisories/GHSA-6qc9-mqvw-jg7x (the first-party advisory referenced by the assigned alias) states the shared-workflow HTTP Request expression attack and patched versions 1.123.67, 2.31.5, and 2.32.1; its npm vulnerability records give <1.123.67, <2.31.5, and <2.32.1. Origin and decomposition: `gh api repos/n8n-io/n8n/pulls/25599` reports merge_commit_sha 608e3bf214328e679c03da3e4a6e9c22ceaac9ca and two commits. `gh api repos/n8n-io/n8n/pulls/25599/commits` gives 7d6023fe3478df86d88f3602f1ea5b53819a050b (parent 0970e4f32cb7efbe257f0ea8105233c3b3a4e179, production change) followed by ad77114af1f8f801fb725f8d1010744baaa4b74a; the latter commit's files endpoint shows it only removes a duplicated test. The contents endpoint at ref=7d6023f shows the newly added `const activeCredTypes = this.getActiveCredentialTypes(node)` and `if (activeCredTypes !== null && !activeCredTypes.has(credType)) continue`, plus a helper that copies unresolved nodeCredentialType. In the validated clone, `git log -L 101,112:packages/cli/src/executions/pre-execution-checks/credentials-permission-checker.ts 608e3bf...` and `git log --all -S 'if (activeCredTypes !== null && !activeCredTypes.has(credType)) continue;' -- ...` both trace the production filter to squash 608e3bf; PR decomposition moves the BIC to 7d6023f. Parent absence: the API says 0970e4f... is 7d6023f's immediate parent, and `git grep -n 'activeCredTypes\|getActiveCredentialTypes' 0970e4f... -- packages/cli/src/executions/pre-execution-checks/credentials-permission-checker.ts` has no match; the parent instead iterates Object.values(node.credentials) and maps every credential ID, so the target ID reaches the access check. Lifecycle: `git show 608e3bf^..608e3bf -- ...credentials-permission-checker.ts` shows the filter landing publicly. `git for-each-ref --contains=608e3bf...` and `git grep` show n8n@2.8.4 lacks activeCredTypes while n8n@2.9.0 contains it, making 2.9.0 the first demonstrably affected 2.x release. Bundle 2d9a2ec... (first contained by n8n@2.15.0) later adds `activeTypes.add(genericAuthType)` without expression resolution; `git log -L 143,150:... 2d9a2ec...` attributes those exact lines to that bundle, and its parent 732f2a3d3ddba59fb6e51bf2534fd33792a2cde3 has no genericAuthType in the checker. Fix: `git diff f69dfc6dd2178a14ea1624d2e1d403c2e755042f^ f69dfc6dd2178a14ea1624d2e1d403c2e755042f -- ...credentials-permission-checker.ts` adds isExpression imports and returns null when nodeCredentialType or genericAuthType is an expression; null makes mapCredIdsToNodes check every referenced credential. Its regression test constructs `genericAuthType: '={{ "httpHeaderAuth" }}'` with victim credential ID and requires an inaccessible-credential rejection. Branch landings are 1cd2c5fb22a906058cc083c3af2d561ce7f4332d (1.x), f6cb6cf3ab177c3740a5ef624b89bae5165405a1 (2.31.x), f69dfc6dd2178a14ea1624d2e1d403c2e755042f (2.32.x), and 2222fe3a6c886a9059f28e1b6d4bdb10ee420624 (mainline). `git grep -n 'isExpression(genericAuthType)' n8n@1.123.67 n8n@2.31.5 n8n@2.32.1 -- ...credentials-permission-checker.ts` finds the guard in all three fixed tags; it is absent from n8n@1.123.66, n8n@2.31.4, and n8n@2.32.0, while the unsafe raw add is present in 2.31.4 and 2.32.0. The resolved fixed-tag commits are ff05cd3be8c4a8f2ac73f42b54f5213493810313, aa3d214338d610300c3c7c70f0ed08e5675bc722, and 7d43cce19523691ee00d89bcc12786fd511d2329 respectively. reasoning: The authorization invariant before 7d6023f was conservative: every credential ID referenced by a node was checked against the workflow's accessible credential set. The BIC optimized away supposedly inactive credentials based on static parameter values, but expression parameters deliberately resolve later. Therefore a credential can be runtime-active and statically omitted, which is the advisory's root cause. The immediate parent lacks the filter and cannot take this bypass. PR #25599 is publicly decomposable: the first member writes all production logic and the second changes only a test, so using squash merge 608e3bf or later bundle 2d9a2ec as the BIC would be larger and causally late. The fix restores fail-closed behavior specifically at the static/runtime boundary by returning null for either expression-selected credential type, forcing every referenced credential ID through authorization. No qualifying AI evidence exists on the true BIC commit object, so the only supported closed verdict is NOT_AI.
